title: Performance Engineering
summary: Compare data layouts, allocation strategies, strides and algorithms with deterministic counters and a simulated cache instead of an unstable stopwatch.
description: Every lesson gives you instruments written in C: operation counters and a small simulated cache. You change a program, predict what the instruments will say, and prove the gain by counting. The course says plainly that a model is not a hardware measurement: the cache is one level, 4 KiB and has no prefetcher, so results show what the model charges for, which is a strong hint about real machines and not a promise. Lessons cover loop order, strides and set conflicts, array-of-structs against struct-of-arrays, arena allocation, choosing an algorithm by input shape, a design comparison where you build two approaches and choose between them with evidence, and a capstone that combines layout, allocation and indexing. Written justifications cannot be graded by a machine; tests check results and counters.
outcomes: Predict and measure cache misses for different access orders and strides with a simulated cache.
Choose between array-of-structs and struct-of-arrays layouts using evidence from access counts.
Replace per-object allocation with an arena and account for system allocations.
Pick an algorithm by input shape and prove the gain with operation counters.
Build two designs with equal results and defend a tradeoff with measured costs, stating what the model leaves out.
